sections.text: This procedure details the steps required to completely check the proper operation and calibration of the RAZOA relay. It is recommended this procedure be carried out on a yearly bases. This work be carried out section of this document is divided into 3 sections.

The first preliminary steps to prepare for relay testing describes the activities required prior to testing. Some of these steps could be performed days before the actual test. The second section
preparation for testing describes the steps to set up the equipment for performing the actual tests. The third section is the actual test.
The document is formatted the way to minimize the possibility of error causing personal injury or damage to equipment.

sections.text: Preliminary Steps to Prepare for Relay Testing

items: Review technical reference material manufacturers manual.
Obtain outage for line protected by this relay.
Check that the bus and line disconnect switches are opened and tagged
Inspect the secondary circuits of CT, VT and all cabling supplying the relay.

Before inserting the test plug into 
the relay, check from the station drawing that the test plug will isolate
Breaker trip coils and transfer trip scheme.
Breaker failure scheme associated with this relay.
Fault recorder, event recorder and disturbance alarm associated with this relay.
Acceleration scheme.
Auto-recloser associated with this relay.
If the test does not isolate one of the pervious steps you have to isolate it.

sections.text: Testing the Relay and the Relay Outputs

items:
Carefully follow the test 
 procedures
Verify the test result match the relay setting .If not consult the technical services.
Test trip all breakers associated with the relay.
Return relay and the associated equipment to service.
This procedure is used to perform off load test.
Look at the EEA panel nameplate and check that EEA system designation nameplate agrees with the line that has been taken out of service.
Using a clip-on ammeter check there is no current flowing in the terminal no. 3, 5, 7 and 9 on the rear side of the test switch.
Using voltmeter check there is no volt on the terminals no. 11, 12, 13, and 14 on the rear side of the test switch.
The P- switch on the relay should always be kept in 01 position when testing RASOA.

sections.text: Over Current Relays IR, IS and IT

items: The over current relay is tested in the same way as the zero sequence relay INS but you increase the current to the terminal 3 and 9 on the test plug until the indication R appears
For over current relay IS inject the current to the terminals 5 and 9 on the test plug until the indication S appears.
For over current relay IT inject the current to the terminals 7 and 9 on the test plug until the indication T appears.

items: Connect the two cases together by using the RTXG connector. Connect terminals RSTN of the test set to the 110 Va.c. output of the Aux. transformer. Connect the test set with the test plug and with the timer as shown in figure (1).
Insert the test plug to the RASOA test switch , then connect the 380Va.c three phase voltage input to the Aux. transformer.

Set the switches: Q in position I., 
 M in position 0, until further notice, P in position I.
Set the product of the S1 and S2 setting equal to the rated current of the RASOA relay.

Turn the main switch H to position I, with switch AF position I, the light emitting diode above AF is lit if all terminals R, S, T and N are supplied with voltage. The light emitting diode remains dark if one or several phases are missing.
The phase sequence in the a.c supply is checked with the switch AF in position 2 the light emitting diode is lit if the phase sequence is RST the diode is dark if the phase sequence is reversed.
Set the switch H to position O. Set the switch F to position RN.
Set the switch Gx and potentiometer Fx at their highest value and GR potentiometer FR in position 0, i.e. the voltage supplied to the relay will lead the current with approx. 90°.
Turn switch M to position 1 then, turn switch H to 1 position.

Reduced the setting of GX and FX one step above the operating value of the impedance relay, which is checked by observing the indication R in RAZOA. Reduce the setting of FX until the relay operates by time delay T4.
Read off the value of GX and FX then turn of the switch H to position 0.
Tests could be repeated in other phase angles with other combinations of GX, FX, GR, and FR.
Repeat steps 7 until 12 for the other type of faults, switch F at different positions SN, TN, RS, ST, and RT.
